growth_story.headline: Income per person in St. Kitts and Nevis grew 3.5 percent a year to 2008 and 1.3 since, as debt, shocks and swings in citizenship-sale money shaped growth.
growth_story.arc: From 1990 to 2008 income per person in St. Kitts and Nevis grew 3.5 percent a year, with building and tourism leading growth by the mid-2000s, even as hurricanes in the late 1990s and the 2005 closure of the sugar industry left the government deeply in debt. Since 2009 growth has averaged 1.3 percent a year. The global downturn brought a recession, with income per person falling 3.6 percent in 2009, and public debt was then restructured under an IMF-supported program agreed in 2011. Money from selling citizenship then fed a building boom, with growth of 5.6 percent in 2013 and 7.5 percent in 2014, and income per person reached its peak in 2019. The pandemic cut it by 15.2 percent in 2020; by 2025 it was back within 0.3 percent of the 2019 peak, while revenue from citizenship sales fell sharply in 2024 after the program was tightened.

threads.title: Sugar ends, debt piles up
threads.text: Sugar had been the islands' main industry for centuries until it closed in 2005, and the government had to service the sugar company's debt. Hurricanes in the late 1990s had already added to a heavy public debt.

citations.title: St. Kitts and Nevis: 2006 Article IV Consultation—Staff Report; Staff Statement; and Public Information Notice on the Executive Board Discussion
citations.quote: In July 2005, the sugar industry—the historical mainstay of the economy— closed after more than 300 years.

citations.title: St. Kitts and Nevis: 2006 Article IV Consultation—Staff Report; Staff Statement; and Public Information Notice on the Executive Board Discussion
citations.quote: The closure has required the government to service the debt of the sugar company (about 29 percent of GDP).

citations.title: St. Kitts and Nevis: 2006 Article IV Consultation—Staff Report; Staff Statement; and Public Information Notice on the Executive Board Discussion
citations.quote: accumulated as a result of a series of exogenous shocks (including three hurricanes in the second half of the 1990s)

threads.title: Global downturn and debt restructuring
threads.text: In 2009 and 2010 tourism receipts and foreign-funded building fell, and the economy shrank. The government then went through an IMF-supported program that included a major restructuring of its debt, including a swap of debt for land.

citations.title: St. Kitts and Nevis: 2011 Article IV Consultation and Request for Stand-By Arrangement—Staff Report; Staff Supplements; Public Information Notice and Press Release on the Executive Board Discussion; and Statement by the Executive Director for St. Kitts and Nevis
citations.quote: Activity is estimated to have declined both in 2009 and 2010, due to a fall in tourism receipts and FDI-related construction activities.

citations.title: St. Kitts and Nevis: 2015 Article IV Consultation and First Post-Program Monitoring Discussions—Press Release; and Staff Report
citations.quote: undertook a major debt restructuring exercise, including a debt-land swap

threads.title: Citizenship sales fuel a boom
threads.text: In the mid-2010s a surge of money from the citizenship-by-investment program paid for a wave of building and government spending. The IMF called the program the main driver of the economy's strong performance in those years.

citations.title: St. Kitts and Nevis: 2015 Article IV Consultation and First Post-Program Monitoring Discussions—Press Release; and Staff Report
citations.quote: Continued rapid inflows under the Citizenship-By Investment (CBI) program have led to a surge in construction activity

citations.title: St. Kitts and Nevis: 2015 Article IV Consultation and First Post-Program Monitoring Discussions—Press Release; and Staff Report
citations.quote: Recent developments suggest increased risks to the Citizenship-By-Investment (CBI) program, the main driver of the economy's strong performance.

threads.title: Citizenship revenue falls back
threads.text: After reforms that tightened the program, money from citizenship sales dropped sharply in 2024. The IMF expects it to stay low, keeping the budget in deficit and public debt rising.

citations.title: St. Kitts and Nevis: 2025 Article IV Consultation—Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Alternate Executive Director for St. Kitts and Nevis
citations.quote: CBI revenue fell to 8 percent of GDP in 2024—from 22 percent of GDP in 2023—due to recent reforms to strengthen the program

citations.title: IMF Executive Board Concludes 2026 Article IV Consultation with St. Kitts and Nevis
citations.quote: Persistently low CBI revenues expected to keep deficits elevated in 2026 and over the medium term; public debt projected to continue rising.

threads.title: Slow, uneven tourism recovery
threads.text: The economy has been recovering from the pandemic and the rise in living costs. Overnight visitors have nearly returned, but cruise arrivals were still below their pre-pandemic level in 2024.

citations.title: St. Kitts and Nevis: Staff Concluding Statement of the 2024 Article IV Mission
citations.quote: St. Kitts and Nevis continues to recover from the pandemic and cost of living crisis

citations.title: St. Kitts and Nevis: 2025 Article IV Consultation—Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Alternate Executive Director for St. Kitts and Nevis
citations.quote: Stayover tourism has almost returned to pre-pandemic levels, but cruise arrivals are still below pre-pandemic levels.

since_last_year.text: In its May 2026 review the IMF reported that money from citizenship sales fell further in 2025, the budget deficit widened and public debt moved closer to the regional benchmark. It says growth slowed in 2025 and expects it to pick up in 2026.

citations.title: IMF Executive Board Concludes 2026 Article IV Consultation with St. Kitts and Nevis
citations.quote: With Citizenship-by-Investment (CBI) revenue declining further, the overall fiscal deficit widened to 11.7 percent of GDP in 2025

citations.title: IMF Executive Board Concludes 2026 Article IV Consultation with St. Kitts and Nevis
citations.quote: public debt edged up closer to the 60 percent of GDP regional benchmark

citations.title: IMF Executive Board Concludes 2026 Article IV Consultation with St. Kitts and Nevis
citations.quote: Economic growth slowed in 2025 but is expected to rebound to 2 percent (y/y) in 2026 and strengthen over the medium term.

growth_story.tension: The IMF says growth slowed in 2025, but the data file shows income per person growing 2.5 percent in 2025, up from 0.1 percent in 2024. The IMF measures total output and the data file measures income per person, yet the two point in opposite directions for the latest year.
